title: Per-symbol timing fabricator and cache-interaction telemetry
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description:
Background:
We need finer-grained attribution for token-level latency and cost that factors in incremental KV-cache influence and request emission timing. Existing request-level spans (API -> runtime -> model) do not capture per-symbol micro-latencies nor the causal relationship between cache hits and downstream token emission delay.

Goal:
Deliver a low-overhead per-symbol timing pipeline that: (1) records microtimings for each emission step (tokenization, model step, KV cache lookup, kernel execute), (2) tags each timing with lightweight cache/hit metadata, (3) ships an aggregated, queriable stream into our metrics/log pipeline for dashboards and cost allocation.

Design summary:
- Tracing model: introduce a short-lived child span type "lexeme.step" per emission token with attributes: lexeme_index, token_id (hashed), step_kind (tokenize|kv_lookup|kernel_exec|emit), duration_ms, kv_hit (true|false), model_variant, route_id, request_sampling_id. Spans must respect trace-context propagation (W3C) so they can be folded into higher-level request traces.
- Sampling strategy: default uniform sampling at 5% of requests, with adaptive sampling triggered by SLO breaches (increase to 25% for affected routes) and a separate low-cost burst capture mode for post-incident debug where we capture 100 requests for 1 minute.
- Cost attribution: derive a simple per-token cost contribution using kernel_ms * hardware_unit_cost + kv_miss_penalty. Maintain an offline mapping that converts aggregate kernel_ms by model_variant and sequence-length class into token-dollar attribution.
- Pipeline and storage: instrumented spans are emitted to our local vector agent which tags and forwards to Kafka topic "telemetry.lexeme-timings.v1". Consumers: (a) clickhouse-aggregator job (hourly rollups per model_variant/route/token_bucket), (b) real-time stream job that computes per-route p50/p95/p99 emission latencies and kv_hit rates (used by console alerting).
- Cardinality controls: token_id must be hashed and truncated (16 hex chars). Additional tags limited to fixed enums. Drop any user-supplied prompt text from spans; only keep fingerprinted prompt bucket id.
- Overhead budget: end-to-end additional CPU should be <1% at 5% sampling, and per-request added latency <0.4ms median.

Implementation plan:
1) Instrument runtime emission path (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3582) to create lexeme.step spans with the minimal attribute set. Feature-flagged behind "lexeme.telemetry.v1".
2) Add a vector/agent config update and Kafka topic creation (infra PR infra#1743).
3) Implement clickhouse aggregator job and add metrics names: redwood.lexeme.emit_ms{route,model_variant,seq_bucket}, redwood.lexeme.kv_hit_ratio{route,model_variant}.
4) Console dashboard: lexeme-level latency heatmap, kv-hit waterfall per model_variant, per-route cost attribution panel.
5) End-to-end perf testing and staged rollout (canary on dev->staging->production routes).

Acceptance criteria:
- Spans emitted for sampled requests contain required fields and are trace-linked to request traces.
- Aggregator produces hourly rollups and stream processing exposes p95/p99 with <2% margin vs raw sampling.
- End-to-end overhead measured and within budget at 10k req/s baseline during load tests.
- Dashboards surfaced in Console show actionable insights and link back to request traces.

Risk & mitigation:
- Cardinality explosion: enforce hashed token_id and conservative enums. If cardinality grows, fallback to route-only aggregation and increase sampling.
- Privacy: ensure no raw prompt content is included; prompt buckets only via hashing. Security review flagged for encryption-in-transit only; KMS concerns considered low.
- Performance regressions: feature gated and throttled via dynamic sampler.

Open design decisions:
- Whether to attribute KV lookup cost to upstream tenant or to runtime infrastructure pool (affects billing). PM to decide by EOD 2026-03-05.
- Whether to store full lexeme traces for 7 days behind paid retention; default is 3 days.
